name: Mount Eerie
label: P.W. Elverum & Sun
lede: Phil Elverum shut down the Microphones in 2003, took the name of the mountain above his hometown and has released almost everything since on a label he runs from his own house.

eras.title: Tuba, then drums, then a four-track
eras.text: Phil Elverum grows up in Anacortes, Washington, under the mountain he will later name a project after. A record-store job, a Beat Happening drummer's seat and a move to Olympia put him in the middle of the K Records world.

years.src: Wikipedia: Phil Elverum · Wikipedia: Mount Eerie
years.h: Phil Whitman Elverum is born in Anacortes, Washington
years.p: He starts on tuba, switches to drums at fourteen and forms a band called Nubert Circus. His father made mixtapes for him and his sister.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's biography has him born May 26, 1978, in the town where he still anchors his whole catalog: the mountain, the ferry, the woods. The project name Mount Eerie comes from Mount Erie, which looms over Anacortes.

Until 2003 he spelled his surname Elvrum. This page uses the newer spelling throughout.

years.h: Love Tara by [[Eric's Trip|fe6365d4-74f3-4706-9aea-d061a394722d]] rewires a teenager's idea of a record
years.p: Elverum found the Moncton band's homemade album through record-store promos. A dog barking and a car passing in the background blew his mind, he told Exclaim!.
years.xp: Elverum told Exclaim! that the four-track, tactile feel of Rick White's recordings has kept shaping how he works. He made a pilgrimage to Moncton in the late 1990s and later made two records with Eric's Trip's [[Julie Doiron|44727d86-a37c-449f-aa91-4a8554127336]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Phil Elverum · Wikipedia: The Microphones
years.h: Bret Lunsford hires him as drummer for D+; the Microphones begin
years.p: Working at The Business record store in Anacortes, Elverum met [[Beat Happening|449e44cb-bcae-4c48-a1af-5d8df0f81456]]'s Bret Lunsford, who recruited him for D+ alongside [[Karl Blau|688d2d9d-8f49-4187-b558-2c961c699ab1]]. The same year he started recording as [[The Microphones|6f2f87e7-3ce9-4f1c-81dd-6f068a78cf26]].
years.xp: Wikipedia puts the D+ recruitment around 1996 and the founding of the Microphones the same year, on cassettes for the KNW-YR-OWN label. His first full albums came later: Tests (Elsinor, 1998), then Don't Wake Me Up and It Was Hot, We Stayed in the Water on K Records.

years.h: He moves to Olympia and records at Dub Narcotic Studio
years.p: Elverum lived in Olympia until 2002, working at a food co-op and recording in [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]]'s studio. By 2000 he was living in the Track House, a hub for local musicians.

eras.title: The record everyone keeps coming back to
eras.text: In Olympia, Elverum records The Glow Pt. 2, the album that makes the Microphones a name. Then he closes the band on a five-track album named for his hometown mountain, and changes the project's name to match.

years.cap: The Glow Pt. 2 (2001), cover art from a 1933-34 Dutch cookbook.
years.h: The Glow Pt. 2 is released on September 11, 2001
years.p: Recorded at Dub Narcotic from May 2000 to March 2001 on 16-track tape, it was released by K Records and Elverum's own P.W. Elverum & Sun. Pitchfork named it the best album of 2001.
years.xp:
Elverum played and produced nearly everything. [[Mirah|e4c226f2-ba57-483f-be6b-3391112244b8]] often came to the early-morning sessions and encouraged him, and [[Khaela Maricich|07d0cdc9-6e87-4645-ba65-a042961c6e7c]], who engineered, is referenced in the songs. Per Wikipedia, the cover art is taken from a Dutch cookbook of 1933-34.

Pitchfork first scored it 9.2, later revised to 9.3. Wikipedia's summary says Elverum himself has called the idea of albums being "essential" a "total myth." It has since been sampled by [[Lil Peep|92da4329-77a4-425c-8e92-4280110cace9]].

years.h: Mount Eerie · the last Microphones album of the 2000s
years.p: Five tracks, 40:51, a life from womb to death sung by different voices as different characters. It was recorded at Dub Narcotic between November 2001 and June 2002. Pitchfork gave it 8.9.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mount Eerie · Wikipedia: Mount Eerie (album)
years.h: "Mount Eerie is a new project. The Microphones was completed"
years.p: Elverum announced the change in September 2003, moved home to Anacortes and started spelling his surname Elverum.
years.xp: He explained the name in a 2014 interview as a way of tying the music to its place. The album and the project both borrow the mountain's name; his themes had moved, per Wikipedia, from recording equipment to weirder, darker, natural ones.

eras.title: Home, a label, a winter in Norway
eras.text: Back in Anacortes, Elverum builds the machinery he still runs himself: his own label, his own packaging, a marriage and a run of records that go from fold-out sleeves to a black metal detour.

years.src: Wikipedia: Phil Elverum · Wikipedia: Geneviève Castrée
years.h: Elverum marries the artist [[Geneviève Castrée|5460ddbb-68c2-491c-a0ad-fafd74d2bd85]]
years.p: They met in 2003 through mutual friends and settled in Anacortes, where they became central to the local scene, including the What The Heck festival.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mount Eerie · Wikipedia: Phil Elverum
years.h: P.W. Elverum & Sun, Ltd. opens its doors
years.p: The label he founded in 2004 would release nearly all Mount Eerie records. Elverum prints, packs and ships the vinyl and merch himself.
years.xp: The same year brought Seven New Songs of "Mount Eerie", Mount Eerie Dances with Wolves (a 12" recorded live to acetate on an Australian tour) and the live triple album Live in Copenhagen.

years.h: "No Flashlight": Songs of the Fulfilled Night · first Mount Eerie studio album
years.p: It arrived in a fold-out sleeve with footnotes, an early sign of how much he treats the object as part of the record.

years.h: Dawn · a winter alone in a Norwegian cabin, in a 144-page book
years.p: Elverum wrote the songs in winter 2002-03 after a breakup, in a remote cabin in Norway. The CD came bound to a hardcover with his journal entries and drawings.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Dawn is Mount Eerie's third full-length, catalog number ELV 017, with [[Karl Blau|688d2d9d-8f49-4187-b558-2c961c699ab1]] engineering. AllMusic, Tiny Mix Tapes and Sputnikmusic each gave it three stars out of five, a rare mixed patch in this run.

q: It's definitely not a black metal album.
years.h: Wind's Poem gets called a black metal album. Elverum disagrees
years.p: Elverum's own verdict on making a "kitschy genre album", as he told an interviewer. He recorded it with [[Nicholas Krgovich|1a90d42f-a474-4904-835b-b2414f89d36c]] in Anacortes, and it scored 8.2 at Pitchfork.
years.xp:
Sessions ran from February 14, 2008 to March 27, 2009 at Nowhere in Anacortes. He cites Xasthur's Subliminal Genocide and Burzum among the sources of the sound, but he rejects the label outright.

On tour he played with Krgovich, [[Tara Jane O'Neil|a9a6334c-1541-4aef-8092-fe743f0df64f]] and Julia Jacklin. One reviewer said the shows delivered distortion "so heavy the walls shook."

eras.title: Fog, fire and a church studio
eras.text: Elverum makes his most atmospheric records at a studio in Anacortes, releases two companion albums in one year and is invited to play for an old hero.

years.h: Clear Moon · recorded over fifteen months at the Unknown
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.3. After Wind's Poem's distortion, it swapped in ominous rumbling and isolated feedback squalls.
years.xp: Recording ran October 3, 2010 to January 7, 2012 at the Unknown, a studio in Anacortes. Elverum chose not to release it as a double album with its companion, feeling that would overwhelm listeners.

years.h: Ocean Roar · the fog to Clear Moon's glints
years.p: Elverum called it the opposite of its sibling: a wall of blue-grey fog, a half-remembered drive to the winter ocean at night. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp: The album runs 38:43 and includes a cover of Popol Vuh's "Engel Der Luft." In October 2012 a 7-inch paired condensed versions of both records, with side B playing every Ocean Roar track at once.

years.h: [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]] picks him for All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: Elverum played Mangum's curated ATP at Minehead, England, and called it an honor to be chosen. [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]] was a band he loved.

years.h: Sauna · "Vikings and zen and real life"
years.p: Recorded June 2013 to August 2014 in the Unknown, a converted church in Anacortes. Pitchfork gave it 8.1 and Metacritic scored it 82.
years.xp: Elverum called it music meant to weigh heavy "like a lot of cold water at night," with the sauna as a place where flames, steam and dim light wipe out ordinary sensation. Some reviewers found the lyrics too literal.

years.src: Wikipedia: Phil Elverum · Wikipedia: Geneviève Castrée
years.h: A daughter is born; Castrée is diagnosed with pancreatic cancer
years.p: After the birth of their child, Geneviève Castrée was diagnosed with inoperable pancreatic cancer, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: The room where she died
eras.text: After Castrée's death, Elverum makes plain-spoken albums in the house where she died. They become the best-known records of his career, and he takes them on the road in churches and small halls.

years.cap: Phil Elverum playing a show in 2010 · Wikimedia
years.h: Geneviève Castrée dies at home in Anacortes, aged 35
years.p: Castrée, a cartoonist and a musician as Woelv and Ô Paon, died of pancreatic cancer. Elverum has said she died at home with him and her parents holding her.
years.xp:
Born April 9, 1981, in Loretteville, Quebec, she published Susceptible in 2012. Drawn & Quarterly published her posthumous A Bubble (2017) and Maman Apprivoisée (2018).

Elverum would make three Mount Eerie albums about her life and death.

years.cap: A Crow Looked at Me (2017), cover photo of Castrée's art studio.
years.src: Wikipedia: A Crow Looked at Me
years.h: A Crow Looked at Me, recorded in the room where she died
years.p: He recorded it from August 31 to December 6, 2016, in his Anacortes home with a single microphone, an acoustic guitar and some of Castrée's instruments. Pitchfork gave it 9.0.
years.xp:
The cover shows Castrée's former studio, with Elverum's hand holding Joanne Kyger's "Night Palace," a poem that mattered to her. Singles "Real Death" (January) and "Ravens" (February 15) came first. Metacritic scored it 93 and it became his best-selling record, per Wikipedia.

He toured North America in April and September 2017 and Europe that November, often in churches and intimate halls.

years.h: Now Only · "part two" of the grief, recorded in the same room
years.p: Recorded March 14 to October 9, 2017, it has nine songs averaging seven minutes. Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and called it "part memoir and part magnum opus."
years.xp: Elverum described it as a shift from raw catharsis to looking at how Castrée persists in his life after her death. It carried the singles "Distortion" (January 17) and "Tintin in Tibet" (February 20).

years.h: Elverum marries the actor Michelle Williams in the Adirondacks
years.p: According to Wikipedia, they wed in July 2018 and moved to Brooklyn, separated in January 2019 and were divorced by November 2019. He returned to Washington state.

years.h: (after) · a Dutch church, November 10, 2017
years.p: A live recording of songs from A Crow Looked at Me and Now Only at the Jacobikerk in Utrecht, during Le Guess Who? Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Nathan Reese wrote that even after so many performances, the songs "sound as raw as they did" when first committed to paper and tape. Tiny Mix Tapes gave it a perfect five out of five.

years.h: Lost Wisdom pt. 2 · recorded in a week with the door open
years.p: Elverum and [[Julie Doiron|44727d86-a37c-449f-aa91-4a8554127336]] made it May 26 to June 1, 2019. Birdsong and jackhammering leak into the tracks because the door stayed open.
years.xp: Doiron wrote the melodies she sang and Elverum wrote the lyrics. It is a sequel to their 2008 Lost Wisdom. Metacritic scored it 79.

eras.title: The Microphones come back, once
eras.text: Elverum revives his old name for a single 44-minute song and a run of shows, then closes it for good with a box set.

years.src: Wikipedia: Microphones in 2020 · Wikipedia: The Microphones
years.h: Microphones in 2020 · one song, 44 minutes 44 seconds
years.p: Recorded between May 2019 and May 2020 and released on P.W. Elverum & Sun under the old name. Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and Best New Music.
years.xp:
Elverum worked the lyrics out by walking around and mumbling them, then wrote them on a nine-foot scroll before recording. The cover is a 1999 photo by [[Mirah|e4c226f2-ba57-483f-be6b-3391112244b8]]. It is explicitly a look back at The Glow Pt. 2.

The revival began with a one-off Anacortes concert in June 2019.

years.h: The box set Completely Everything, 1996–2021 is announced
years.p: It was billed as the final Microphones retrospective. Limited tour dates in 2021 and 2022 preceded the project's end.

eras.title: Night Palace
eras.text: After five years with no Mount Eerie album, Elverum delivers a 26-song double record from his home studio, pitched as a spiritual successor to The Glow Pt. 2.

years.h: Night Palace is announced with "I Walk" and "Broom of Wind"
years.p: Stereogum reported the 26-track album as Mount Eerie's first in five years. Indigo Free directed the video for "Broom of Wind."

years.h: Night Palace · 26 songs, 80 minutes 47 seconds, on P.W. Elverum & Sun
years.p: His first double album and longest Mount Eerie record, recorded between 2022 and 2024. Elverum works from a home studio on Orcas Island, a ferry ride from Anacortes.
years.xp: The title comes from Joanne Kyger's poem, which appeared on the cover of A Crow Looked at Me. Elverum told Exclaim! the record is edited down from far more recordings, and that an 80-minute album of one mood "would suck."

years.h: Night Palace is pitched as the sequel to The Glow Pt. 2
years.p: Elverum's own summary of the album, per Stereogum: a mix of meditation, decolonization and backwoods protest songs recorded on reel-to-reel.

q: Feels like a culmination of his work over the past 25 years.
years.src: Wikipedia: Night Palace · Album of the Year
years.h: Pitchfork gives Night Palace 8.3 and ranks it No. 7 of 2024
years.p: Pitchfork's Daniel Bromfield wrote that it feels like a culmination of Elverum's work over 25 years. The album also landed at No. 1 on The Atlantic's year-end list.
years.xp:
Metacritic collected 14 scores for an 86 ("universal acclaim"), per Wikipedia. Stereogum also ranked it No. 7. Dissent: Slant gave it 60, Paste 75 and Rolling Stone 80, according to Album of the Year.

AllMusic's Heather Phares said it "holds a special place in his discography."

years.h: Release shows in Brooklyn and Los Angeles
years.p: Elverum played Warsaw in Brooklyn on November 19 and the Bellwether in Los Angeles on November 21.
